```artifact
Feature: Doorstop Requirements Management

  Scenario: Store Requirements in a Permanent and Secure Manner
    Given a new requirement is created
    When the requirement is saved
    Then the requirement is stored in a permanent and secure manner

  Scenario: Handle Change Management of Requirements
    Given a requirement is created and saved
    When a change is made to the requirement
    Then the change is associated with the developer who made it

  Scenario: Associate Requirements Changes to Existing Developer Identification
    Given a requirement is created and saved
    When a change is made to the requirement by a developer
    Then the change is associated with the developer's identification

  Scenario: Scalability of Doorstop to Support Thousands of Requirements
    Given Doorstop is configured to support thousands of requirements
    When a large number of requirements are created and saved
    Then Doorstop handles the requirements without performance issues

  Scenario: Lightweight Installation Method
    Given Doorstop is installed using the lightweight method
    When the installation is complete
    Then Doorstop is fully functional and requirements can be managed

  Scenario Outline: Store Requirements in a Permanent and Secure Manner with Examples
    Given a new requirement is created with the following details
      | Requirement ID | Requirement Description |
      | <req_id>        | <req_description>        |
    When the requirement is saved
    Then the requirement is stored in a permanent and secure manner

    Examples:
      | req_id | req_description          |
      | 1      | This is a test requirement |
      | 2      | This is another test requirement |
      | 3      | This is a requirement with a very long description that exceeds the maximum allowed length |

  Scenario Outline: Handle Change Management of Requirements with Examples
    Given a requirement is created and saved with the following details
      | Requirement ID | Requirement Description |
      | <req_id>        | <req_description>        |
    When a change is made to the requirement
    Then the change is associated with the developer who made it

    Examples:
      | req_id | req_description          |
      | 1      | This is a test requirement |
      | 2      | This is another test requirement |
      | 3      | This is a requirement with a very long description that exceeds the maximum allowed length |

  Scenario Outline: Associate Requirements Changes to Existing Developer Identification with Examples
    Given a requirement is created and saved with the following details
      | Requirement ID | Requirement Description |
      | <req_id>        | <req_description>        |
    When a change is made to the requirement by a developer
    Then the change is associated with the developer's identification

    Examples:
      | req_id | req_description          |
      | 1      | This is a test requirement |
      | 2      | This is another test requirement |
      | 3      | This is a requirement with a very long description that exceeds the maximum allowed length |

  Scenario Outline: Scalability of Doorstop to Support Thousands of Requirements with Examples
    Given Doorstop is configured to support thousands of requirements
    When a large number of requirements are created and saved
    Then Doorstop handles the requirements without performance issues

    Examples:
      | number_of_requirements |
      | 1000                    |
      | 2000                    |
      | 3000                    |

  Scenario Outline: Lightweight Installation Method with Examples
    Given Doorstop is installed using the lightweight method
    When the installation is complete
    Then Doorstop is fully functional and requirements can be managed

    Examples:
      | installation_method |
      | default              |
      | custom               |
      | manual               |
```
